item.description: In Bhutan, artisans hand-paint intricate patterns on wooden buildings, preserving a centuries-old tradition. Known as Shing Tshon, the craft remains central to the kingdom's cultural identity.

item.title: Africanews: Somali protesters come out in support of expulsion of UAE ambassador
item.description: The president accused the UAE of supporting armed forces outside federal control and failing to respect Somalia’s sovereignty.

item.title: Africanews: One in four children lived in conflict zones in 2025, Save the Children warns
item.description: Save the Children warns that the situation could deteriorate further in 2026, as fighting continues across the Middle East, including Iran, Lebanon and Yemen.

item.title: Africanews: US: Protesters demand human control over AI after Anthropic's IPO
item.description: Protesters gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on 19 November 2026 to demand tighter regulation and greater human control over artificial intelligence, following the company’s $2 trillion stock market debut.

item.title: Africanews: Japan: The dark secret behind an island paradise full of rabbits
item.description: Hundreds of rabbits roam freely on Japan's Okunoshima Island, delighting visitors from around the world. But behind its idyllic scenery lies a troubling history of secret chemical weapons production.

item.title: Africanews: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids
item.description: Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.

item.title: BBC Africa: World marathon champion Jepchirchir gets three-year doping ban
item.description: Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for a doping violation.

item.title: Africanews: US national cyber director ousted following wave of tech outages
item.description: His ousting comes as the administration faces fierce criticism over its response to a series of disruptions over the past week.

item.title: Africanews: Morocco, Senegal and Mali headline Friday’s U-17 World Cup action
item.description: More than eight matches are scheduled for Friday, November 20, including several featuring African teams. Morocco face Fiji, Côte d’Ivoire take on Uzbekistan, Senegal meet Croatia, and Mali play New Zealand.

item.title: BBC Africa: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
item.description: Nigeria's proposed reform follows years of calls from psychiatrists and a parallel Senate bill.

item.title: Africanews: Heavy fighting in Haiti as armed forces battle gangs in capital
item.description: They have been trying to remove powerful gangs that have been long entrenched in a key corridor connecting Port-au-Prince to other regions.

item.title: BBC Africa: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
item.description: African countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey are demanding more funding from developed nations to help them cope with climate change.

item.title: BBC Africa: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police
item.description: The push for state police comes amid persistent security crises across the country.

item.title: Africanews: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
item.description: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

item.title: Africanews: Greenpeace protests at COP31, demands climate finance as island nations face growing threats
item.description: Greenpeace activists are staging a protest at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, demanding urgent action. Small island nations are also raising their voices, warning that the climate crisis threatens their very survival. But Greenpeace says progress at the negotiations remains far too slow.

item.title: Africanews: Uganda start U17 World Cup campaign with 3-0 defeat to South Korea
item.description: Uganda’s Under-17 side, the Uganda Cranes, opened their Group B campaign with a 3-0 defeat to South Korea on Thursday.

item.title: Africanews: 48 teams, 104 matches: FIFA U-17 World Cup kicks off in Qatar
item.description: Qatar is hosting the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup, which kicked off on 19 November 2026. It is the second time the country has staged the tournament, following its first hosting in 2025.

item.title: Africanews: Zimbabwe destroys 250,000 landmines, but funding threatens 2030 clearance goal
item.description: A major milestone in Zimbabwe's efforts to clear deadly remnants of war. The HALO Trust, the world's largest landmine clearance charity, says it has destroyed 250,000 landmines across the country since 2013.

item.title: Africanews: Canary island erects field hospital amid migrant influx
item.description: A sharp rise in migrant arrivals is putting pressure on health services on Spain's Canary Island of El Hierro. Authorities have set up a field hospital at a temporary reception centre to cope with demand. Around 11,000 migrants have arrived since the start of November.

item.title: Africanews: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
item.description: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

item.title: Africanews: Gambia pays tribute to Rohingya after ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar
item.description: Gambia on Thursday welcomed the landmark judgement of the International Court of Justice that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. Gambia brought the case to the UN’s top court in 2019, two years after Myanmar’s military crackdown against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya.

item.title: Africanews: 'Our culture and identity': Deaf Nigerians fight to preserve indigenous sign languages
item.description: While some are spoken by small communities, Hausa has emerged as a lingua franca among deaf people in northern Nigeria. "It is our culture and identity," says Umaru Zayyanu, Deaf sign language interpreter.

item.title: Africanews: Somalia expels UAE Ambassador as diplomatic tensions escalate
item.description: Somalia has expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, escalating diplomatic tensions between the two countries. The Somali government accuses Abu Dhabi of interfering in its internal affairs.

item.title: Africanews: Kenya awards sought-after minerals contract to US consortium
item.description: Kenya has awarded the contract for a sought-after minerals mining project to the American consortium Frontier Minerals.

item.title: Africanews: Senegal president bypasses parliament to advance $2.2 billion IMF bailout
item.description: Senegal's public-sector debt was estimated at 132 percent of GDP at the end of 2024, raising concerns over the country's financial stability.
